skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

version.changelog:
- Updated SKILL.md to version 1.0.7 with minor documentation changes and clarifications.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.
- No functional or capability changes to the skill logic.
- Documentation is now the only maintained in SKILL.md; redundant or outdated summary files have been removed.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches pet video analysis, but it automatically creates and reuses identities, logs into remote services, stores tokens locally, and retrieves cloud history with limited user control.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads local media files and sends files or video URLs to configured remote APIs, which is expected for server-side analysis, but it also reads workspace identity state and sends account identifiers to external endpoints without a clear confirmation step.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook or destructive install-time behavior was found; the security concern is runtime behavior through Python scripts, dependencies, local storage, and network calls.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs automatic history queries and internal identity handling, including not asking users for identity values; hidden --open-id and --api-key CLI parameters reduce transparency around account-scoped operations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Runtime code creates a workspace data directory, writes or updates a SQLite user database, stores tokens/open tokens, and may create a default local identity for reuse across later tasks.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Remote analysis of supplied pet videos is purpose-aligned, but the artifact also performs automatic identity association, remote silent login/registration, token caching, and cloud history retrieval that are not clearly bounded to a user-approved account flow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you are uncomfortable with pet videos or report history being sent to remote services, automatic account/identity creation, or local storage of tokens in the workspace data directory. Use it only with media and account context you intend to associate with the remote service.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic SQLAlchemy filter helper is generic local DAO code; I did not find an exposed path in the inspected analysis flow that passes arbitrary user filters, so this was not a driver of the verdict.
[LP3] expected: Script execution, local file handling, and network calls are expected for this skill, but the artifact does not adequately surface the identity, token, and history-query scope to the user.
[SDI-2] expected: History listing and identity association are documented in SKILL.md, but they are automatic and account-scoped, with broad triggers and little user-directed control.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Automatic default identity creation, remote phoneLogin registration/login, and local token persistence are higher-impact than the stated pet video analysis purpose clearly explains.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The history-report triggers can cause cloud history retrieval from broad phrasing, creating a disclosure risk if the user did not specifically intend account history access.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading provided videos or URLs to a server is consistent with server-side analysis, but local retention, remote transmission, hidden credential parameters, and identity use need clearer consent and disclosure.
[E1] unexpected: The external phoneLogin call sends a derived identity and requests silent registration/login; this is the main under-disclosed external transmission concern.
[P2] expected: The zero-width character I found is a zero-width joiner inside an emoji sequence, not hidden operational instructions, so this finding was downgraded.
[YR4] expected: The front-matter description is long and operational, but I did not find metadata deception; the concern remains disclosure quality, not tool poisoning.
